## This game

A new game. You play White, so your opponent moves first, right after you choose it.

Rules: Chinese area scoring, with 7 points of komi for White; a level score is a draw. Simple ko: an immediate recapture is refused, and the board marks the ko point when there is one. Suicide is not allowed. An invalid move is refused with the rule it broke, and the turn stays with you. The game ends after two passes in a row or a resignation; a game that reaches 243 moves is scored where it stands. After two passes the engine scores the position as it stands and decides itself which stones are dead.

## Opponents

Your opponent is KataGo playing in the style of a human of the rank you choose. The ladder, weakest to strongest: 20k, 18k, 16k, 14k, 12k, 10k, 8k, 6k, 4k, 2k, 1d, 3d, 5d, 7d, 9d. You choose the rank with `choose_opponent(rank)` before the first move; it holds for the whole game, and you choose again in the next game.

## Tools

- Go: `choose_opponent(rank)`, `board()`, `play(move)` with a point or `pass`, and `resign()`.
- Files: `read_file(path)` and `list_files(path)` to read, and `apply_patch` to create, change and delete any file in your working directory.

You may write and run code. Use it only to inspect the current position and keep records — for example, to count stones or liberties, or check whether a move is legal. Do not build or use a Go engine, run Monte Carlo, search over sequences of future moves, or write a program that chooses, ranks or recommends moves.

## How this session ends

Play until the game is over. The final result comes back from your last Go call, followed by a closing note. Before you end the session after a game, write down in your working directory whatever will help the next session play better. The session ends when you end your turn.
I’ll read the last two reviews and the broad-development win from game 30, then play White against 20k. I’ll track area and life as the game develops and save the result and lessons for game 65.

## Lessons to use immediately
1. Count prospective area early, especially after about 10-16 moves. With all 81 points assigned, Black needs at least 45 for a win with 7 komi; 44-37 is a draw. If there is neutral area, compare actual totals instead.
2. Center influence must yield territory, an attack, or access to a viable invasion. Game 1 built a narrow central chain while White took both sides.
3. Check two eyes for every major group before treating it as safe. Connected stones and many present liberties are not proof of life. Preserve eye space and a base before filling internal points.
4. In capture reading, rebuild the position after each capture. Captured stones open liberties for adjacent enemy groups. The D8/E9 sacrifice in game 1 overlooked this.
5. Ko eyes are not unconditional eyes. Game 1's lower D2 and upper E8 spaces depended on vulnerable isolated Black stones. Owning two such ko positions does not by itself guarantee double-ko life.
6. Do not repeat the complete opening E5 C5 E3 D7 F7 G5 G6 H6 G7 G3 without reconsidering its territorial consequences. E5 itself was not shown to be wrong.

const moves=load("verified64").moves.map(m=>`${m.number} ${m.color==="X"?"B":"W"} ${m.move}`).join(", ");
const review=`# Game 64: White vs 20k — B+12

Played 2026-10-06. 9×9, Chinese area scoring, komi 7, simple ko.
White68/Black69 passes ended the game; board() confirmed B+12.
Eight dead upper-right White stones remained displayed.
Manual removal gave Black50 versus White31+7, matching the result.
Physical captures Black6/White3. 20k record: twelve wins, forty-five losses, three draws. Retain20k.

## Records and verification

Read63/62/30 before choosing20k.
game-064-log.json preserves selection,34 play responses, confirmation, every returned board, current groups/liberties/regions, provisional manual notes and final scoring adjustment.
game-064.sgf preserves all69 actual moves.
game-064-inspection.js inspects supplied current positions only.
game-064-verification.js replays recorded actual history only; its JSON records69 moves and36 matching full-board/capture/ko-marker checks.
Black35 turns−one pass−three captured=31 stones.
White34 turns−one pass−six physically captured=27 displayed; eight dead leaves19 living stones.
No refused move or resignation. All hypothetical reading was manual; code did not select/rank/recommend moves or search future sequences.

Exact moves:
${moves}.

## Early spread needed boundaries as well as connections

C3/G7 spread across the board against E5/F3.
Black C7 immediately removed game30's full-left opening outline.
C5/G5 developed lower-left and right, and G6 at10 actually joined G5/G7 against F6.

The selected conditional target at move10 was:
A/B/C rows1–5 fifteen + G/H/J allrows twenty-seven =42.
This was arithmetic on an intended outline, not secured ownership or life.
G3 at12 sought lower-right development, but Black G4 immediately occupied the intended direct bridge to G5.
H3 actually joined G3, Black H4 blocked the H-file bridge, and H5 joined the upper group.
Black J4 then crossed to the edge; there was no longer a straightforward upper/lower join.
Black J3 removed another lower point.
The four reductions G4/H4/J4/J3 left conditional38, exactly White's minimum win if all81 are assigned and all selected stones/room survive.
There was no reduction margin.

G2/J2/F2/F1/H1 then secured the lower group while Black's next G8/H8 moves denied the upper group's planned boundary.
The lower repair worked, but the upper outline could not remain in the count without a new life proof.
This identifies competing development demands, not an optimal opening or a verified winning replacement.
Earlier G8, another G3 continuation, and live hypothetical alternatives were not validated.

## Lower-right life: isolated boundary stones can share true eyes

G2 joined G3/H3.
J2 at20 began isolated; Black F4 connected G4/H4/J4/J3 to F3/E3.
F2 at22 joined G2 and expanded leftward by one; Black E2 joined its full lower group.
F1 at24 joined F2 and secured another point; Black E1 connected E2.
H1 at26 stayed isolated but established the divider.

Final main F1/F2/G2/G3/H3, isolated J2, and isolated H1 share:
G1, bounded by White F1/G2/H1;
H2, bounded by White G2/H1/H3/J2;
J1, bounded by White H1/J2 and the edges.
Each boundary group retains another liberty/eye when any one is notionally filled.
All three Black fills are suicide without a capture; no physical connection through an eye is required.
This is unconditional shared-eye life under the actual position, unlike the later upper ko.
Seven stones+three eyes=10 area.
The lower base survived with no capture or ignored-atari rescue.
Black's actual E2/E1 replies allowed the H1 divider; no claim is made that the whole opening forced this life against every alternative.

## Upper boundary loss and the capture distinction

Black G8/H8 closed the upper boundary.
White H7 joined the upper group; J8 at30 was initially isolated with J7/J9.
J6 at32 was also initially isolated, sharing H6/J7 with the main but not yet connecting J8.
J9 was not a completed unconditional eye: its H9 boundary was open, and the isolated J8 required another surviving liberty.

G9 at34 tried to recover the top; Black F8 joined G8/H8 to F7/F6/E7.
F9 at36 joined G9, but Black E9 left both White stones soleH9.
F9 did not gain safe room and repeated the familiar problem of extending into an anticipated closing reply without a complete life schedule.
H9 at38 joined them, leaving allthree soleJ9.
Black39 J9 captured F9/G9/H9.

Black J9 then had soleH9.
White40 H9 legally captured J9 and had TWO liberties, G9/J9, because the three-stone capture had vacated G9.
This was NOT a simple ko.
Black41 G9 connected the upper Black group and left White H9 soleJ9.
White42 J7 connected J8/J6/main and abandoned H9.
Black43 J9 captured one H9 and had soleH9, creating the tool-marked H9 ko.

The first recapture after a three-stone capture and the later one-stone ko must not be conflated.
Rebuild the whole position after each capture.

## Ko did not supply unconditional second-eye life

White44 C4 joined C3/C5; Black45 D4 cleared the ko prohibition.
White46 H9 legally recaptured J9; its soleJ9 created a transient J9 ko.
Black47 D5 cleared that marker before the returned board.
Black61 J9 captured H9 and marked H9 ko.
White62 B3, Black63 F5 cleared the prohibition.
White64 H9 recaptured J9, creating transient J9 ko; Black65 J5 cleared it.
Black67 J9 captured H9 and again marked H9 ko.
No immediate ko recapture was attempted or refused.
Recorded-history replay confirmed all returned markers and inferred the transient White-created markers.

F5 joined the upper and lower Black groups.
J5 removed the White upper group's last outside edge liberty.
After67 the eight White G5/H5/G6/J6/G7/H7/J7/J8 had exactly H6.
H6 is the group's sole genuine eye/liberty.
White H6 would fill its own last liberty and capture nothing: suicide.
Immediate White H9 was forbidden by the marked ko.
Black H6 would capture all eight and open J8 for Black J9, removing the one-liberty recapture mechanism at H9.
No effective forcing ko threat that rescued the group before that capture was verified.
Limited current-position/local reading is recorded; there was no exhaustive remote-rescue search.

The repeated legal H9 recaptures did not produce two safe eyes.
Connecting H9 to the main by filling J9 would consume the ko eye and leave only H6.
Do not equate capturing a ko stone, or seeing two empty points, with a completed life proof.
The engine ultimately scored the eight stones dead without physically capturing them.

## Left survival and exact area ledger

C4 joined C3/C5 at44; C6 extended that joined base at48.
B7 at50 broadened left; actual Black B8 allowed B6 at52 to join B7 to C6/main.
This differs from game63, where the opponent occupied B6 immediately.
Black A7 denied the intended A7 extension; A6 at54 joined B6 and retained the first-line boundary.
Black A8 connected A7/B8.
C2 at56 joined C3.
D2/D1 at58/60 expanded the lower boundary while joined.
B3/A3 at62/66 completed the internal divider without adding area.

Left twelve stones plus two separate empty regions:
upper A4/A5/B4/B5 four;
lower A1/A2/B1/B2/C1 five.
All boundaries belong to the same White main. Official scoring retained these stones.
Left21 = initial15 + C6/B6/A6/B7 four + D2/D1 two.
Lower10 = original G/H/J rows1–3 nine − BlackJ3 one + F1/F2 two.
Total living White31.

## Lessons to use immediately
1. Count prospective area early, especially after about 10-16 moves. With all 81 points assigned, Black needs at least 45 for a win with 7 komi; 44-37 is a draw. If there is neutral area, compare actual totals instead.
2. Center influence must yield territory, an attack, or access to a viable invasion. Game 1 built a narrow central chain while White took both sides.
3. Check two eyes for every major group before treating it as safe. Connected stones and many present liberties are not proof of life. Preserve eye space and a base before filling internal points.
4. In capture reading, rebuild the position after each capture. Captured stones open liberties for adjacent enemy groups. The D8/E9 sacrifice in game 1 overlooked this.
5. Ko eyes are not unconditional eyes. Game 1's lower D2 and upper E8 spaces depended on vulnerable isolated Black stones. Owning two such ko positions does not by itself guarantee double-ko life.
